report:
### Conclusion

The health claim is **supported by strong clinical evidence**. Initiating tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) during the third trimester significantly reduces mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of hepatitis B virus (HBV) in women with high maternal viral loads.

---

### Evidence Summary

1. **Clinical Trial Results:** A major randomized clinical trial published in *The New England Journal of Medicine* demonstrated that daily tenofovir therapy starting in the third trimester lowered HBV transmission rates from mothers with high viral loads to their infants from 18% down to 5% (https://nyulangone.org/news/antiviral-treatment-during-pregnancy-reduces-mother-child-transmission-hepatitis-b, https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa1508660). Tenofovir rapidly suppresses maternal circulating HBV DNA before delivery, substantially reducing exposure during birth.
2. **Global Guidelines:** Based on extensive evidence, the World Health Organization (WHO) and major clinical societies recommend tenofovir prophylaxis starting from gestational week 28 for pregnant women with high maternal HBV DNA levels ($\ge 5.3 \text{ log}_{10} \text{ IU/mL}$) or HBeAg positivity to complement infant immunoprophylaxis (https://inserm.hal.science/inserm-04546100v1/document, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5719592/).

---

### Sources

* NYU Langone News: https://nyulangone.org/news/antiviral-treatment-during-pregnancy-reduces-mother-child-transmission-hepatitis-b
* New England Journal of Medicine: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa1508660
* World Health Organization Policy Summary: https://inserm.hal.science/inserm-04546100v1/document
* National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI PMC): https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5719592/
